templates.title: OpenCode (Native Anthropic)
templates.instructions: For OpenCode 2. Place at ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json. Pick this variant for Claude models — it passes through extended thinking, prompt-cache hints, and server-tool blocks unchanged. We register the gateway under its own provider key, `{{provider_key}}` — named for your tenant and provider, so a project config never merges into another provisioning's entry — on OpenCode's built-in Anthropic package rather than overlaying its `anthropic` provider, which isolates the gateway from OpenCode's preset Anthropic config. A project config lives at `.opencode/opencode.json`. OpenCode also reads your home-directory config, and two of its settings outrank a project's: a provider policy (`experimental.policies`, or a v1 `enabled_providers` list) that leaves `{{provider_key}}` out, and a per-agent model pin. Both forms therefore pin every built-in agent to this provider — `build`, `general`, `summary` and `compaction` to the default model, `plan` to the plan model, `title` and `explore` to the fast model (each the default model until an admin fills that slot) — replacing a model you had pinned to one of them; an agent still pinned to another provider — one of your own, or a pin under the older `agent` key — is kept, and `ssai provision` and `ssai status` name it. A home-directory policy that denies `{{provider_key}}` still wins over a project. The home-directory form therefore adds an `experimental.policies` statement allowing `{{provider_key}}` — at the end of the file's statements, or in place of one it already has for that provider: OpenCode applies the last matching statement of a file, so it lifts a `deny` on `*` written before it; a deny placed after it still wins, and `ssai provision` and `ssai status` name it. In a project, `ssai run opencode` uses the project config in place of the home-directory one, so it is not affected. The home-directory form turns OpenCode's self-update off (`"update": "disable"`); OpenCode honours that key only there. A credential stored for `{{provider_key}}` through `opencode providers login` takes precedence over the `apiKey` below. Session sharing is off (`"share": "disabled"`) and OpenCode's own web search is disabled and not offered to the model — the agent searches through the gateway's MCP web tools when the workspace has them. An admin who wants either back can edit this template.

templates.title: OpenCode · MCP only (static key)
templates.instructions: For OpenCode 2. Merge into ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json alongside any existing provider block. No LLM key is minted in this flow — OpenCode keeps its existing provider config. Each server is exposed to the model tool by tool (`"codemode": false`), so the gateway's tool policy sees every MCP call by name. Session sharing is off (`"share": "disabled"`) and OpenCode's own web search is disabled and not offered to the model, so the agent searches through the gateway's MCP web tools; OpenCode's model calls keep going to the provider you configured. An admin who wants either back can edit this template.
